summary: For the 2026 NASA Space Apps Challenge, we created an educational video. The video covers four abandoned NASA projects that have finished their mission. We focused on making the video engaging and interesting for young children ages 8-14, similar to something a science teacher might play for the class. Rather than throwing out random and hard-to-understand science terms, we simplified it to help kids grasp the concepts better. Our story helps bring four historic NASA machines to life - explaining what each mission was for and the impact it had on our trajectory as humans. Apollo 11 Eagle,  LCROSS, InSight Lander, and NEAR Shoemaker helped make these scientific discoveries possible. The hardware, effort, dedication, and time that went into these machines deserve to be remembered. Our take on the Abandoned but not Forgotten storytelling topic is what we believe will get young viewers genuinely interested in space exploration.
details: The project we created helps kids ages 8-14 stay engaged and interested in space science and the NASA equipment that helped make history. It is a simple video presentation very similar to ones a science teacher may play in class, but this time it's much easier to follow along with. It helps introduce the future generation to space exploration and the dedication, commitment, time, and effort that went into it. This video sparks interest, hope, and curiosity in young learners, inspiring the next set of scientists, engineers, and astronauts. We used Canva to help put all our clips together, NASA's Images and Video Library, and YouTube clips. Our project is different and creative because we designed it from a kid's perspective. Being teenagers ourselves, we know how boring it is to sit in a science class watching boring videos that seem to last forever. We considered the questions "What do kids really want to watch?" and "What made the science videos so boring in the first place?" By combining clear and small explanations, animated videos, along with voiceovers we helped turn a boring science class into a fun educational day!
